label: late original-phase inputs and the <DEL> step (end of encoding)
explanation: Fires only while the sequence is being read in: original-phase steps from t>=3 (mostly t>=4) and the <DEL> step (74% of <DEL> steps active, 39% of mass). Never fires at t=0-1, almost never at t=2, and is essentially silent for the whole copy phase (1 activation out of 2.7M copy steps). In the original phase the firing rate rises with position (t=3 19%, t=5-8 50-70%). The strongest activations ramp up over the last few inputs and peak at <DEL>. It fires more on first occurrences of a token (in_first=1 holds 91% of mass) and is weaker on repeats. Magnitude and rate also depend on which tokens came first: sequences whose first tokens are a, y, 0, c, d, q, s or u fire much more often (restricting to those raises precision to 0.88 but cuts recall to 0.35). So the positional window is necessary but not sufficient, and many in-window steps stay inactive. The simple predicate covers 96% of activation mass at precision about 0.62.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: 0, a, y, d, c, q; least: 3, r, z, o) and the current input token, by step (t=2: o, z, 2, 3; t=3: o, z, 2, 3; t=4: o, z, 2, 3); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=5, phase=1.
